note: Published examples the engine is checked against. Each is a published tool or paper example, not plant data. Values under 'published' are transcribed from the research dossier of 2026-09-26; values under 'authored' are inputs the example does not state and this product chose.

molycop.source: Moly-Cop Tools (Sepúlveda), BallSim_Direct base case: its Data_File (breakage parameters, fresh-feed size distribution, classifier constants), its Reports (classifiers performance, mass balance around the classifiers, stream size distributions, mill power) and its Flowsheet; the BallParam_Direct Reports for the second classifier state. Two public copies of the Moly-Cop Tools document agree on every value used. Methodology page 03 states the comparison.

parameters.note: The BallSim_Direct Data_File's own values. beta2 is read from a cell printed apart from its label (UNVERIFIED reading); 3.5 to 4.5 moves the net energy from 7.12 to 7.45 kWh/t.

authored.why: The work index equals the reference work index, so the selection function applies unscaled. The head grade only sets the two-mineral split, whose density (2.66 t/m3, not the published 2.80) enters only the volumes. Installed power is unlimited, so the solver meets the published P80 and circulating load: they are inputs, not results. Below the last sieve (38 um) the feed is extended by the Gaudin-Schuhmann slope of the last two sieves. The mill's mixer structure is the engine's.

molycop.tolerance_basis: PE-08 as first written (design commit 45f8d67, 2026-09-26): net specific energy within 20%, set before the first run.
molycop.previous: Until 0.08.000 the oracle used BallParam_Direct's parameter guesses, an authored Rosin-Rammler feed, sharpness 1.66, 35% overflow solids and an authored geometry, and compared 9.13 kWh/t with the gross 8.56 (review of 2026-10-02, E-05 and E-08).

gmg.source: Global Mining Guidelines Group, GMG01-MP-2021, sections 4.2.1 and 4.2.2; methodology page 09.

laplante.source: Laplante and Staunton, Gravity recovery of gold, an overview of recent developments (AMIRA P420B), Figures 10 and 11, read from the images; the GRG model of Laplante, Woodcock and Noaparast (1995) as Vincent (1997, McGill M.Eng. thesis, chapter 5) states it; Snip's measured GRG by size from Vincent's Table 5.1. Methodology page 06 states the comparison.

grg.why: The published example's GRG by size is not printed (only 87.7% of the discharge GRG below 150 um). The oracle declares Snip's measured GRG (Vincent 1997, Table 5.1, the second test), which Vincent calls extremely fine; its -25 um class spreads log-uniformly over 10 to 25 um, the laboratory Knelson's lower limit.

authored.ore: Quartz with 60% silicate_fe and 2% pyrite (SG 2.79); 80.4% of the gold as GRG, the rest in pyrite. The mill, fresh feed and cyclone sharpness are the gold case's; installed power is unlimited so the solver meets the published P80 and load.

fit.why: The Knelson's maximum recovery per pass is fitted at the printed 30% row and labelled fitted; the other rows are predictions.

laplante.tolerance_basis: Set before the first run (2026-10-02) and stated on methodology page 06; a miss is recorded, not tuned away.
laplante.why: Until 0.08.000 this was a trend oracle comparing the gold case's recovery of all its gold with the published GRG figures. It now runs the published example's inputs with an ore of 80.4% GRG and compares GRG recovery and GRG circulating load at each bleed.

zandrivierspoort.source: Muthaphuli, P. (2014), Production of pelletizing concentrates from Zandrivierspoort magnetite/haematite ore by magnetic separation, J. S. Afr. Inst. Min. Metall. 114(7), read on scielo.org.za.

grinds: The ball-mill circuit targeted 80% passing 75 um and reached only 66.8% (an in-house screen); the concentrate came from rougher, cleaner and recleaner LIMS stages.
The 75 um concentrate was IsaMilled to 80% passing 45 um and cleaned in three LIMS stages: a regrind product, not a finer primary grind.

zandrivierspoort.why: A trend oracle: the published ore is magnetite with haematite, and the engine's case is magnetite in an iron silicate. The engine reaches 45 um by a finer primary grind with two drums, where the published product is a regrind with three cleaning stages, and its 75 um grind is finer than the published one. The direction and the size of the grade step are compared, the levels and the silica are shown beside them, and the rougher stage is compared at 75 um only, the one campaign that had it.
